"Rules? Alright, - the secretary replied. - It is played with a 36 card pack. Players are dealt by two cards and then they count points. Counting is easy: six is six points, seven is seven points, and so on until ten, which is ten points. Jack is two points, Queen is three, King is four and Ace is eleven points. 

If after the first deal I have 21 points, I automatically win, no matter how many points you have. Sorry mate: my pack - my advantage. But if I do not get 21 points with 2 cards, then each of us can take by 1 card from the pack. By the way, one can take up to five additional cards. Here you go. There is an opportunity to collect 21 points. If a player has more than 21 points - it is called an overshoot. But you can refuse to take an additional card when you think you may collect more than 21 points. 

After both of us stop taking cards, the game is over. We show our cards to each other and compare collected points. If the numbers of points are equal, then it is drawn. If anyone has more points and there is no overshoot, that one is the winner. That's it. 

In general, the rules are not complicated, but sometimes it's hard to realise them at once. You'll get it when you play."

<clr>Every Maloq loves to...<clrEnd>
loc.172.0:
- Fine, so you have passed the test, - Bobchinsky went on.
- And now, are your going to sign the lease documents for Hillside? - you asked.
- No.
- What do you mean no? 
- That's what I mean. I am not authorised to deal with leases.
- Who is authorised then? - you asked.
- Head of the transportation shop, who else?
- Why head of the transportation shop?
- Because that's his business, - the housemaster replied, crumpling the papers you just brought and throwing them into the trash can.
- Why you've just thrown away the papers I brought to you?! - you exclaimed.
- These papers had nothing to do with leasing. - was the answer.
- Then what has?
- Please contact head of the transportation shop regarding all issues. By the way, - the housemaster glanced at his computer screen, - he has just arrived at the ministry and is now in his office. And now excuse me, I have work to do.
- But what about...
- Leave the room please.
"Damn those bureaucrats" - you said to yourself, holding back dirty language.
loc.173.0: - So, hmmm. You've got [p22]. Bad, really bad. According to the tables, you are not a trustworthy member of the galactic society. I am very sorry, but any further co-operation is out of the question. Those who do not pass the test, can not work with the ministry of Rectal Island, - the housemaster said, shaking his head.
loc.174.0:
Hopeless to obtain the Hillside lease papers, you returned to your ship, sadly started the engines and flew away from Rectal Island. 

You mission is failed.
loc.175.0:
- Well, only out of respect for you, I rather have a look at some papers, - Bobchinsky took out a large pack of documents and began searching them.
After several minutes he took out a sheet and said:
- According to paragraph 31-345, clause 4, individuals, mentally retarded from the birth, can operate in the ministry without successfully passing the test. In such case they are required to pay an amount, proportional to amount of missing points, required to pass the test. In your case it is {(20-[p22])*12} cr.
loc.176.0: You stand outside at the entrance to the pink building. There is a plate above the doors: "Ministry for various affairs of Rectal Island". To the North there is a small lake. You starship is shining in the sun nearby.
loc.176.1: You slowly moved around the building. You found nothing interesting on your way. Except for the windows. But they were all too high to have a look inside or climb in. After you completed a full circle, you arrived at your starting point.
loc.176.2: You roamed about the ship, but haven't found anything useful or at least anything that could be carried in your hands.
loc.178.0: You got knee-deep into the water, but could not extract anything but mud from the bottom. Wait! Something is moving in your hands. It is a small <clr> bloodsucker<clrEnd>.
loc.180.0:
As soon as you entered, a heated person ran up to you.
- Fish samples. Have you brought them? 
- Sure. Here they are, - You handed your three-eyed trophy to the official.
- What is it?
- A fish.
- It has three eyes... Why didn't you disembowel it? - the man said and began shaking the fish.
And then the fish, which turned out to be alive, shivered, slid from the hands, broke the window glass and got out to the street. Surprised, you and the official run to the window and watched the fish jumping towards the lake. 
- Are they all like that at your warehouse? We don't deliver anything like that.
- What warehouse? I came here to discuss lease of Hillside. 
- Lease? You should have said from the very beginning. Instead you come here with a fish... For how many years you want the lease?
- Fifty, - you said calmly
- No problem, - the head of the transportation shop sat at the table, filled in several blanks and handed them over to you. - Alright, you can go now. Do not disturb me anymore.
Satisfied, you headed to your steel eagle and in a few minutes left Rectal Island in a jolly mood and with the lease documents!
loc.181.0: You got into your lovely starship and left Rectal Island. That was right. Meddling with papers is not appropriate for a real ranger.
loc.182.0: The housemaster watches you carefully. He must be waiting for you to pay him.

After you cheerfully went down the stairs, you found yourself in the basement and suddenly stepped on your shoelace. The brave ranger sprawled out on the floor like a medusa on the pavement. You stood up, shook the dust off and, oh god! Instead of the expected tidy room you were looking at a ragged basement with a huge hole in the middle. The Registry is anywhere but here. Looks like it was transferred to another room... Or the bureau was sucked into this hole. Right down to hell!!!

You looked at the commandant, and he only smiled, exposing his only three rotten teeth. Then he suddenly changed his expression and shook his finger at you. Looks like it was the middle finger.

- What do you means? - you said.
- Have you registered?
- As a ranger?
- Do you always answer with another question? 
- Why do you ask?
- Young man, you are beginning to annoy me - leave the room and close the door. 
To avoid further problems, you carefully closed the door, although you wished you could slam it.

"And she means that" - you thought descending on the floor.

"Here for you. Yeah, Charlie, Yes. No! I'm not buying the chrysanthemum. No. The wife have not called. No. Fine. I write him down in the register. That's it."
